Adaptive COVID-19 Treatment Trial (ACTT)-et randomiseret studie af behandling af indlagte patienter med COVID-19 i Europa
summary: Projektet har internationalt scope og undersøger muligheden for behandling af indlagte patienter med COVID-19, hvor sygdommen har udviklet sig til alvorlig lungebetændelse. Projektet vil undersøge behandlingsmuligheder med blandt andet remdisivir, som er udviklet til behandling af andre virus. I forsøget vil man behandle allerede indlagte patienter med kendte antivirale produkter, og målet vil være at COVID-19 patienter kan behandles hurtigt og ud fra en allerede sikker bivirkningsprofil.

title: A nationwide study exploring immunological mechanisms in childhood
summary: Projektet undersøger forekomsten af relativ milde forløb med COVID-19 blandt børn og unge (0-17 år). Projektet vil kortlægge de kliniske og immunologiske værtsresponser hos gruppen og vil identificere forskellige niveauer af immunstimulerende - eller undertrykkende cytokiner, for derefter medicinsk at kunne målrette behandling til at lette sygdomsforløbet hos hårdt ramte patienter i alle aldre.

title: Antivirale midler der hæmmer replikation af COVID-19
summary: Projektet undersøger mulighed for behandling af COVID-19 med allerede kendte anti-virale præparater. I forsøget vil man behandle indlagte patienter med kendte antivirale forbindelser, der hæmmer replikation af COVID-19, og på den måde sikre at nuværende COVID-19 patienter kan behandles hurtigt og ud fra en allerede sikker bivirkningsprofil.

title: Konsekvenser af coronavirus for gravide, fødende og deres nyfødte børn
summary: Projektet vil undersøge COVID-19s indvirken på gravide, fostre og nyfødte børn ved hjælp af indsamlede prøver, som kan afgøre mulig genetisk påvirkning af infektionen. Projektet kan give fundament for evidensbaseret rådgivning til gravide.

title: A simple pandemic ventilator for critical situations
summary: Formålet med dette projekt er at afhjælpe dels manglen på respiratorer til COVID-19-patienter og dels manglen på rutineret respiratorpersonale. I fase 1 fremstilles en nødrespirator, som kan sættes i produktion og tages i anvendelse, hvis der skulle komme mangel på traditionelle respiratorer. I fase 2 undersøges en software knyttet til nødrespiratoren, som kan rådgive sundhedspersonalet i deres beslutninger og dermed gøre nød-respiratoren brugervenlig for respiratorpersonalet.

title: Behandling og forebyggelse af svære lungemanifestationer af COVID-19 med Senicapoc (COVIPOC)
summary: Projektet undersøger, om behandling med stoffet senicapoc kan mindske behovet for brug af respiratorer under COVID-sygdomsforløb. Projektets formål er at undersøge, om man ved at behandle kan hindre fremkomst af akut luftvejssyndrom og hindre lungeskader ved COVID-19-infektion. Projektets impact kan være en aflastning af sundhedssystemets ressourcer under COVID-19

title: ANTI-COVID19: Functional protective antibody determinants during and after SARS-CoV-2 (and other CoV) infection to define and predict individual post-infection immunity, flock immunity and guide blood bank sero-treatment
summary: Projektet omhandler immunitet, herunder muligheden for at undersøge specifikke antistoffer dannet i COVID-19 patienter under og efter sygdomsforløbet (både svære og milde sygdomsforløb). Projektet søger at undersøge, om de antistoffer som dannes i patienter under COVID-19 kan booste immuniteten hos nye patienter eller patienter i risikogrupperne, og på den måde understøtte behandlingen af næste bølge af COVID patienter.

title: Unexpected high risk of severe COVID-19 infection in patients with hypertension and diabetes
summary: Projektgruppen undersøger baggrunden for, om der er en mulig sammenhæng imellem højere risiko for COVID-19 blandt patienter med hypertension og diabetes. Patienter i disse risikogrupper behandles ofte med de samme typer af medicin, og dette registerstudie vil forsøge at afdække baggrunden for den øgede følsomhed for COVID-19. Projektet vil kunne give ny viden i forhold til at revidere retningslinjer og give bedre rådgivning til patienter i de to risikogrupper.

title: COVIDTESTS - Rapid and affordable Point-of-Care diagnostics for SARS-CoV-2 virus and COVID-19 diagnosis and management.
summary: Projektgruppen vil fremstille nye diagnostiske værktøjer i form af tests, som nemt kan udføres hvor som helst. Testene vil tillige kunne aflæses indenfor 30 min, og være billigere end nuværende tests. Impact af projektet vil være, at flere patienter kan testes for COVID-19, og at testene kan udføres såvel i akutmodtagelser som uden for hospitalerne.

CoroNAT: Coronavirus neutraliserende antistof terapi
summary: Projektet vil undersøge udviklingen af gode neutraliserende antistoffer hos SARS-CoV-2 smittede. Specielt vil studiet analysere, om både personer, der har haft svære symptomer og om personer med ingen eller meget lette sygdomstegn, danner neutraliserende antistoffer. Ydermere vil projektet isolere og karakterisere de bedste neutraliserende antistoffer for at kunne undersøge, om man enten kan bruge de antistoffer i behandlingsøjemed, eller hvordan man kan inducere sådanne antistoffer ved en fremtidig vaccination.

title: COVID-19 monitorering med måling af C3d, antistof og RNA kopi nummer i blodet mhp på afklaring af om fatalt forløb relaterer sig til immunrespons eller virusload og om antistof respons regulerer eller beskytter.
summary: Projektgruppen vil undersøge, om patienters antistof og immunforsvar er afgørende for infektionens alvorlighed og patientens overlevelse. Hvis dette er tilfældet, vil blod med meget antistof fra raskblevne tidligere patienter kunne bruges til at mildne sygdomsforløbet hos nye patienter ved en transfusion. Indtil en vaccine er til rådighed, er dette en måde at give patienter beskyttelse gennem en passiv immunisering med de rigtige antistoffer.

title: Forståelse af smitteveje gennem sekventering og analyse af coronavirus genomer
summary: Projektet vil udvikle og implementere metoder, der muliggør hurtig fuld-genom sekventering af coronavirus prøver patientnært regionalt og nationalt og at sikre, at sekvensinformation kobles med klinisk og epidemiologisk viden som beslutningsstøtte for offentlige myndigheder.

title: Hurtig og sikker diagnostik i forbindelse med Covid-19 pandemien 2020
summary: Kombinationen af de tre testsystemer, projektet udvikler, kan bidrage til at løse de aktuelle problemer vedrørende opskalering af testkapacitet og testhastighed, samt udvælgelse af egnet testmateriale. Projektet arbejder med 4 PCR baserede metoder, to kantitative (qPCR og ddPCR), en high throughput PCR, og en hurtig enkeltanalyse PCR, som kan levere svar på 10 minutter. Målet er, at der kan anlægges en langt mere aggressiv teststrategi, uafhængig af de eksisterende forsyningskæder.

title: Iltbehandling til COVID-19 patienter med livstruende lungesvigt
summary: COVID-19 patienter er i risiko for at udvikle et akut og livstruende lungesvigt. Tilkobling til en respirator og behandling med ilt er livreddende. Ilt er et lægemiddel og har dermed såvel gavnlige som skadelige virkninger. Projektet vil give oplysning om den rette dosering af ilt til de mest syge COVID-19 patienter og vil dermed kunne bedre prognosen.

title: Individualiserede kirurgiske cancerforløb under corona-epidemien via anvendelse af danske registre
summary: Projektgruppen vil via maskinlæringsmodeller, der bygger på danske registerdata, identificere cancerpatienter, der er i høj risiko for at få et kirurgisk kompliceret behandlingsforløb herunder intensiv indlæggelse. Deres behandlingsforløb under coronapandemien kan rettes mod at forberede dem til kirurgi via optimering uden for hospitalet.

title: Lungeultralydskanning til monitorering af indlagte patienter med COVID-19 infektion
summary: Projektet vil undersøge, om man ved brug af en simpel lungeultralydskanning tidligt i indlæggelsesforløbet kan finde de patienter med COVID-19 infektion, som udvikler svært lungesvigt med behov for respiratorbehandling. Projektet vil kunne hjælpe til en tidligere og mere målrettet diagnostik og behandling af de COVID-19 patienter, som er i højst risiko for at få livstruende lungepåvirkning.

title: Machine-learning in COVID-19: Assessing immunopathology and genetics for tailored care and optimized resource usage
summary: Projektet bruger kunstig intelligens til at forudsige sygdomsforløbet for COVID-19 patienter. Baseret på journaldata, genanalyser (helgenom sekventering) samt detaljerede undersøgelser af immunforsvaret, udvikler projektet en model, der kan forudsige, hvilke patienter der får behov for intensiv og respirator behandling. Projektet vil muliggøre hurtig risikovurdering af indlagte COVID-19 patienter mhp. tidlig og skræddersyet behandling. Dette kan bedre den enkelte patients mulighed for overlevelse og optimere ressourceforbruget. Herudover afdækkes betydningen af genetik og immunforsvar ved COVID-19, så nye behandlingsmuligheder kan identificeres.

title: PRESORT - Cost efficient pre-screening system for virus infection
summary: Projektets mål er at udvikle en simpel og prisbillig test til øjeblikkelig og følsom detektion af sygdomsudvikling for patienter under mistanke for virusinfektion -en point-of-care test til tidlig forudsigelse, før kontakt med hospitalet. Testen baseres på en kombination af celle tælling i blod og detektion af nanopartikler i spyt og udvikles på basis af et eksisterende prototype apparat.

title: Targeting aging in COVID-19 patients to prevent respiratory failure
summary: Dødeligheden hos 80-årige COVID-19 patienter er ca. 100 gange større end hos 30-årige patienter. Dette projekt vil behandle ældre patienter med et B-vitamin lignende stof samt forstå hvilke faktorer, der gør ældre sårbare overfor COVID-19. Samlet kan projektet give en mulig behandling af COVID-19 og forståelse for, hvorfor ældre er særligt sårbare overfor denne virus.

title: A first-of-its-kind spectrometer for investigating electronic properties of materials in the range of the electromagnetic spectrum from 450 nm to 2200 nm
summary: No spectrometer has the performance needed to expand our understanding of how near-infrared light interact with materials. Thus, we will build a spectrometer that can provide quantitative data on how materials and molecules interact with the electromagnetic radiation with a wavelength from 800 nm to 2200 nm. A range that is vital in telecommunication, for understanding rare-earth elements, for guiding rare-earth separation, when making next generation contrast agents for optical bioimaging, and designing new diagnostic assays. The spectrometer will advance our research in organic dyes, lanthanide photophysics, and silver nanoclusters, and can potentially be commercialized offering the capability to research groups around the world.

title: Unveiling the secrets of the enigmatic myosin-binding protein C
summary: Myosin-binding protein C  -MyBP-C-  is a protein that is essential for normal cardiac and skeletal muscle contraction and relaxation. Despite its importance, significant gaps in our understanding of MyBP-C functionality remain. The present proposal aims to clearly define its molecular and cellular regulation. Specifically, in aim 1, we will test the hypothesis that MyBP-C critically modulates the conformation of another key muscle protein, myosin, and subsequently, its energy demand. In aim 2, we will investigate how MyBP-C has adapted and evolved among species and whether this has implications on muscle homeostasis and metabolism. The derived knowledge of our studies will provide basic biology insights and will be precursor to the design of targeted therapies for cardiac and skeletal myopathies associated with mutations in MyBP-C. As I have recently relocated from the UK, this project will also allow me to fully implement a successful and competitive  muscle biophysics  research programme in Denmark.

The lost art of petrography in geosciences
summary: "I hereby apply for support to purchase a state of the art polarization microscope for my research group. In recent years, much of the scientific progress in the field of geology has been driven by the development of new technology, and an ever-increasing analytical precision. However, this focus on cutting edge methods, has resulted in a neglect for the fundamental importance of understanding the petrography and mineral relations in rocks; leading to several examples of outright misinterpretations in recent high-profile literature. Although my research interests are diverse and include projects ranging from defining the meteorite building blocks of the Earth, to the formation of the first continents, to mineral deposits in Greenland, and ongoing development of novel carbon capture and storage protocols, all of these topics have petrography as their common denominator. Hence, the ambition of my research team is to emphasize first-order principles, in order to conduct robust science, by comprehensive documentation of the rock microtextures prior to embarking on more advanced analytical procedures. In this way, I hope to contribute to re-establishing rigorous petrography, as the starting point for research in my field."

title: DECODENSE: Mean-Field Density Matrix Decompositions
summary: The DECODENSE project is concerned with the machine-learned acceleration of Kohn-Sham density functional theory, KS-DFT. Today, KS-DFT constitutes the most versatile and popular computation tool for simulations of molecular systems and solids. By means of a basis of spatially localized molecular orbitals, I am proposing a novel partitioning of the central 1-electron reduced density matrix at different levels, by which total molecular properties may be decomposed into contributions associated with individual bonds and atomic centres. Upon introducing the new decompositions, my project is concerned with how the results of decomposed KS-DFT theory may be leveraged in the application of machine learning to quantum chemistry. I present preliminary results in support of my main hypothesis, namely, that training of machine learning models on decomposed - i.e., atomic - rather than molecular data may facilitate faster learning rates. In turn, this will allow for faster and more accurate machine-learned KS-DFT models, which are bound to have a significant impact on chemical and materials sciences in the years to come.

Coherence and disorder in light-driven phase transitions
summary: The ability to use short flashes of light to control a materials phase and properties has opened up a new route to controlling a material s properties, yet the mechanisms that enable phase control are poorly understood. The aim of this project to explore how vibrational coherence, generated when a solid absorbs a femtosecond pulse of laser light, can be used to control and manipulate the material s properties. Specifically, we aim to demonstrate if coherent is responsible for transient phases, how coherence is lost and if it can be controlled, and how transient states grow in space and time. Our work will combine low temperature, ultra-fast pump probe spectroscopy with time-resolved X-ray scattering using X-ray lasers to gain insights into the macro- and nanoscopic properties of transient phases.

summary: This project aims at disclosing mechanistic details underlying the response of human cells to adverse stress-conditions. This is in part achieved by regulating the activity of RNA-binding protein LARP1, which in turn impacts ribosome homeostasis and hence cell energy expenditure.

title: Mood synchronicity, collaboration media, and task outcomes.
summary: This project aims to explore how shared mood influences different types of collaborative tasks. More specifically, the project explores how the characteristics of different communication media moderate the relationship between shared mood and coordinated behaviors.

title: Fluidic Force Microscope for Single-Cell Manipulation and Analysis
summary: Cells are heterogeneous and understanding their differences at the single-cell level can assist in the effective development of multifunctional drugs, understanding the development of neurodegenerative diseases and physiochemical properties of cells. Effective and minimally invasive delivery of cargo such as drugs, followed by extraction of selective cellular content is of high interest. We aim in close collaboration with our research partners to use fluidFM to manipulate and analyse single cells exposed to novel multifunctional drugs, oligomers expected to play a role in the development of neurodegenerative diseases, and metabolic intervening origami structures for production of biochemicals. Furthermore, in close collaboration with the leading fluidFM expert, we will develop new methodology, namely high-resolution surface charge mapping tools for understanding the properties of the cell membrane. However, the developed methodologies are not exclusive to cellular studies but can be used on practically any surface.

title: Ethnic minorities in the Danish higher education system. A study on the intersection between ethnic and social inequalities with specific attention to written language skills.
summary: The project will explore, which ethnic inequalities exist in the Danish postsecondary education system, both with regard to entry into and success within higher education and thus aims to close a gap in the research landscape. Above and beyond, it will study the intersection of ethnicity with social origins in these inequalities and assess in how far ethnic inequalities are actually social inequalities. The project also aims at breaking new methodological paths for inequality research by combining register data with data on the quality of written language based on natural language processing methods   i.e. automated text analysis. This will enable the project to study writing skills, a core meta-competence needed in higher education, as a mechanism that can amplify ethnic and social inequality. Applying these methods, the project aims at being the first research group that contributes comprehensive evidence on the importance of writing skills for the generation of inequalities in higher education using high quality large-scale data and a broad assessment of writing skills.

title: Detailed signaling profiling of G protein-coupled receptors
summary: The overall aim of the current project is to determine the signaling profile of G protein-coupled receptors in much greater detail than previously possible using novel biosensors and the instrument applied for.

title: Aoptical furnace for quantum materials discovery

The research is linked to the opening of the ESS-neutron-lighthouse center  Magnetism and Quantum Materials. It is  a strongly interdisciplinary project bridging physicists and chemists and combining many experimental techniques with theoretical modeling. The optical furnace will be an important tool in the expansion into solid state chemistry by KU-Chemistry and QMAT. Its impact will be geared by a new position as well as by some exclusivity in the early access to ESS: from the opening of ESS in 2023 and two years on, the design team  encompassing QMAT members  will have exclusive access to a large fraction of the experimental time at the instrument. This will provide a golden opportunity for Danish researchers to become leaders in this field, provided we are ready when the opportunity opens.

Wars, Pandemics, and the Human Mind: Competing Conceptions of Trauma in the 21st Century. Analyzes how and why concepts of  resilience  and  moral injury  reframe trauma and reconfigure the way states and societies manage effects of extreme events.
summary: The project will provide a comprehensive theoretical appraisal of the way trauma is conceptualized and governed today, both in relation to armed conflicts, humanitarian crises, and global emergencies such as the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Using extinct diversity of Asian wild Bos to guide wildlife conservation and improve cattle
summary: The cattle-like wild oxen species banteng - Bos javanicus and gaur - Bos gaurus are in a centuries long population decline as well as greatly understudied. Most populations are extinct and the structure and diversity of the original as well as modern populations are unknown. This project will generate full nuclear genomes from museum specimens of extinct gaur and banteng populations, and in combination with modern data from the host institution, investigate past and present structure and diversity, as well as evolution across time and geography. This information will in collaboration with IUCN be used in conservation efforts of both species. The project will further identify specific genes under selection over time, these gene variants may be useful adaptations that can be used in modern cattle industry. Such genes and their implications will be studied in collaboration with the Danish Centre For Food And Agriculture, for potential optimisation of health, production and sustainability in the industry. In short, using museum specimens to investigate natural history and evolution, with implications for wild life conservation and cattle industry.

title: Using biophysical pharmacology to elucidate the conformational dynamics of the human serotonin transporter
summary: The human serotonin transporter, hSERT, has profound therapeutic implications, yet the molecular basis behind its physiological function is still largely unknown, which is mostly due to experimental challenges. We have solved these challenges. The aim of this project is therefore to use this opportunity, to perform advanced characterizations of hSERT structure-function relationships. Site-selected insertion of non-canonical amino acids and attached transition metals will enable us to perform intra-molecular, distance-dependent FRET measurements. With this molecular ruler, we will  walk  around in SERT and measure interrelated distances and how they are impacted by conformational changes that control the transport process. This tool can also localize the binding site for potassium. The reconstitution of hSERT into lipid vesicles will enable us to elucidate the interplay between sodium and serotonin co-transport and the potassium counter flux. Together, our results will elucidate SERT function at a hitherto unprecedented level of detail.

title: Tools for High-Throughput Screening of Hybrid Quantum Devices
summary: The synthesis of dissimilar materials, such as metallic superconductors matched to semiconducting crystals, has led to hybrid devices with hitherto unseen quantum properties. This has opened the door not only for the exploration of topological condensed matter physics, but also for the creation of complex, more functional devices that will be operated at high frequencies and find use in quantum-technology applications such as quantum simulation and quantum computing. Hybrid devices inherit their superconducting properties through the proximity effect, resulting in high-frequency behaviour that is accessible only at sub-kelvin temperatures.  We propose a shared cryogenic screening setup that is capable of characterizing a wide variety of quantum devices down to temperatures as low as 0.1 kelvin and in magnetic fields up to 2 tesla, with a diverse user base of solid-state researchers including academic and private stakeholders at NBI, Microsoft, QDevil, etc. An automatic load-lock will allow the quick exchange of sample holders, which will be designed to be compatible with user requirements, allowing a smooth cycle of devices between fabrication, characterization, and eventual operation in existing dilution refrigerators. Low- and high-frequency measurements will be supported by up to 24 cryogenic wires and coaxial lines, and a 8-channel arbitrary waveform generator. The setup will be managed and maintained consistent with NBIs nanofabrication suite.

title: The Missionary Dictionary: Native Words, Spanish Concepts, and Pre-Hispanic   Paganism
summary: When sixteenth-century Spanish-imperial missionaries arrived in America to Christianize the indigenous population, they faced a linguistic barrier of unanticipated proportions, making one tool indispensable: the dictionary. The missionaries crafted dictionaries of indigenous languages based on the groundbreaking Spanish-to-Latin dictionary by Spanish scholar Antonio de Nebrija. Because the missionaries focused on translating from the Spanish and Latin vocabulary of Nebrija to indigenous languages, this project proceeds from the hypothesis that many non-Christian religious terms attested in the missionary dictionaries and believed to be of pre-Hispanic origin may actually be innovations introduced into indigenous languages from a Mediterranean pre-Christian, pagan, vocabulary. The aim of the project is therefore to systematically examine non-Christian terminology in missionary Nahuatl and Quechua dictionaries and how that terminology was used for portraying pre-Hispanic religious life in Spanish, Nahuatl, and Quechua texts. For each term confirming the hypothesis, the project will show how missionary dictionaries produced as much as they recorded indigenous languages, changing our views of pre-Hispanic religion and society and indigenous American history.

title: TESCAN Scanning Electron Microscope
summary: Acquisition of state-of-the-art TESCAN Scanning Electron Microscope, SEM, and detector.

title: Socio-economic Effects of Vaccines    Research Infrastructure - SEV
summary: SEV will collect, digitize, and uncover unique historical data regarding U.S. vaccine interventions during the mid-20th Century. SEV will allow us to study how exposure to vaccines affects socioeconomic outcomes, human capital, and sentiments towards public health interventions both in the short and long-run. Vaccine trials, such as the Salk Polio Vaccine Trial of 1954, and government programs, such as the Polio Vaccine Assistance Act of 1955 and Vaccine Assistance Act of 1962, provided idiosyncratic access to vaccines for some populations. The goal is to create a database including vaccine trials, surveillance of disease and vaccine coverage, and government vaccination programs from these archival resources. SEV will fill a gap in knowledge surrounding the socioeconomic effects of polio eradication and broader social savings attributable to the introduction of new vaccines during the 1950s and 1960s by supporting statistical and econometric analyses and the creation of high quality peer-reviewed academic papers.

title: Resurgence and Brane-quantization in  Topological Quantum Field Theory
summary: The overarching goal of this project in mathematics and mathematical physics is to advance our understanding of topological quantum field theory  by developing a synthesis of the new theories of resurgence and brane-quantization.  The attainment of the proposed goals will be of potential foundational importance for quantum theory.

title: Resisting Ghettos: State-led Gentrification and Community Organizing in Danish Social Housing
summary: Focusing on the so-called Ghetto Plan and the grassroots network Almen Modstand in Denmark, this project aims to answer two research questions: How are social housing, marketization, and governance interlinked in the Ghetto Plan? How does the Ghetto Plan affect social housing residents in their everyday lives and how do they resist the policy and its consequences? Answering these questions with an interdisciplinary approach, the project seeks to contribute to debates about gentrification, territorial stigmatization, and resistance in and beyond urban studies.

title: Profiling of drug candidates and materials in biological systems
summary: The aim of the project is to investigate biological responses in cell cultures mediated by new chemical entities and new materials for drug delivery and targeting.

title: Predicting Effective Digital Transformation Factors for SMEs in a Pandemic
summary: Following the onset of COVID-19 and the subsequent lockdowns, businesses are struggling for survival. Identifying and predicting the most effective actions is critical for the continuity and recovery of Small Medium Enterprises  SMEs  during economic disruptions. Technological enablers, such as data-driven advertising, is a crucial aspect of businesses  resilience. Uncovering new economic opportunities due to unprecedented market challenges through digital technologies can be an essential surviving factor, especially for low-tech companies. This project seeks to retrospectively analyze such transformations during the COVID-19 crisis by collecting evidence from real-world case studies and a large sample of business owners to systematically derive reliable recommendations. We propose a mixed-methods investigation among SMEs owners to predict the effect of data-driven advertising on firm performance, learning from this lockdown data. Two large-scale cross-sectional studies will be supported by insights from case studies. The study will assess the resilience and discovery of new markets across SMEs and their relationship to, among others, online advertising, people development, and the use of technology. Participants  N 1,447, globally distributed  have already been identified through the academic data collection platform Prolific. Data will be analyzed using Structural Equation Modelling, which allows making predictions  e.g., which practice will significantly affect resilience , allowing to differentiate conclusions across demographics  e.g., size, industry . Consequently, we will provide evidence for effective and productive practices to cope with an economic downturn and individualized business recommendations on optimizing the use of scarce resources.

title: Politics of the European Green Deal: What is the Role of Missions?
summary: The aim of the fellowship is to explore multi-level governance challenges related to top-down directionality setting of the European Green Deal and bottom-up experimentation promoted through missions in the environmental domain.

title: Novel in vitro assay platform for environmental toxicology at Aarhus University
summary: Establish a novel high-throughput in vitro screening assay platform for forefront research in metabolomics and environmental endocrine disruption.

title: Multi-electrode array, Neurobiology Research
summary: We wish to apply for a multi electrode array  MEA system shared between four neurobiological research groups doing neurobiological research within the fields of stroke, Parkinsons disease and autoimmune encephalitis.

title: Low-Temperature CO2 Valorization
summary: I will develop highly effective hydrogenative CO2 valorization processes at exceptionally mild conditions using a novel combination of an ionic liquid that chemically traps CO2 and a catalyst that activates H2. This combination provides a synergistic system capable of transforming the CO2 to formic acid or other organics under very mild conditions.

title: Long-read sequencing to explore fundamental mechanisms in biology and disease
summary: Acquisition of a cost-effective Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read sequencing machine to unravel novel and previously undiscovered genetic traits, genome biology and cellular mechanisms.

title: Improving the science quality of the Hertzsprung SONG telescope in the Stellar Observations Network Group
summary: The goal of the present application is for Aarhus University to maintain the leading position within a broad range of research activities, from stellar structure and evolution to detailed measurements of exoplanet properties. One of the prime infrastructure facilities that is maintaining our capability to obtain state-of-the-art data is the Stellar Observations Network Group, which at present includes three nodes with a total of four telescopes. Many researchers and students in Denmark, Spain, Australia, China and USA are regular users of SONG and the community is growing, and so is the number of papers published based on SONG data. It has also become clear that SONG is used to support space observations - from TESS and Kepler and in the future from ESA PLATO - and observations done at other ground-based telescope facilities. The aim of application is to perform a complete upgrade and maintenance in order to significantly improve the quality of the facility as well as opening up for improved observations. With the upgrades and repairs, we expect the Hertzsprung SONG telescope to see a huge improvement in the technical performance, operational stability and data quality that is expected to ensure a constant flow of state-of-the-art measurements  in the next decade. The upgrade will provide optimal conditions for the combined observations with the new SONG telescopes in Australia. The upgrade will also allow a better implementation of coordinated observations of oscillating stars and exoplanet transits with the TESS space mission observations.

title: Highest resolution trace gas measurements from ice cores
summary: In the past 10 years, we have been very successful implementing continuous methane concentration measurements from ice cores. We have been pioneers collaborating with Picarro industries. Today the methods we developed are copied in all major ice core laboratories worldwide. We continue developing and improving the methods expanding also to other trace gases. At arm s length is a campaign for measuring the 2500m of ice core from our current Greenland drilling project EGRIP reaching about 80kyr back in time. In the next 5 years the international drilling project EPICA Oldest ice in Antarctica will surface core that is up to 1.5 million years old. We are the designated measuring institute for that core. Our pioneer Picarro instruments for on-line methane measurements are reaching their end of lifetime. With this proposal, we seek funding for a replacement instrument with improved capabilities that can also be used for fundamental research on processes of gas occlusion in ice.

title: High resolution measurements of greenhouse gas dynamics in temporarily stratifying lakes
summary: To gain high resolution data on greenhouse gas dynamics in lakes vulnerable to climate change impacts and so better predict and ameliorate potential positive feedbacks with climate change.

title: Functional root traits of wetland plants
summary: The project aims at unravelling longitudinal depositions of suberin, lignin and wax in the outer cell walls of root of wetland plants, including rice.

title: European Social Survey 10th round
summary: The aims of the European Social Survey is to measure and explain how the European people s social values, cultural norms and behaviour patterns are distributed, the way in which they differ within and between nations, and the direction and speed at which they are changing.

title: Equipment to understand the effect of peripheral calcium-sensing receptor  activation in general physiology.
summary: We have found that calcium-sensing receptor activation thresholds differ across various epithelia and organs and this has profound consequences for our understanding of how this biological system works and how it contributes to maintain electrolyte balance. To examine these effects in detail, we are in particular need of a system that can analyses many electrolytes simultaneously and with auto sampler capacity.

title: Environmental gas-exchange system to study leaves in variable external conditions
summary: We apply for an environmental chamber system to measure photosynthesis and transpiration and to challenge plant leaves with different light intensities, CO2 levels and temperatures. This will allow us to assess water usage and the checkpoints for adjusting long-distance transport by connecting the system to our custom-made chamber in an X-ray imaging device. With the this gas-exchange system, we can adjust intensity and spectral quality of the light and modify temperature and CO2 levels in the chamber.

title: Empire without Alternative? Autocratic Power and Inevitability in the early Roman Empire
summary: "The project aims to question the assumption that the Romans of the early Empire were unable to imagine alternatives to one-man rule; unable to imagine that history could have taken a different course and that things could have turned out differently. It has two primary research objectives: to explore how the claim that one-man rule was inevitable functions as a premise within imperial ideology, and to investigate how alternatives to autocracy are activated, or shut down, in historical texts from the early imperial period. Additional aims include to advance scholarly collaboration among the universities of Aalborg, Newcastle, Heidelberg, and Yale; establish an international, cross-disciplinary research group working on autocratic ideology and legitimation; stimulate public debate on autocratic ideology in contemporary Danish society, esp. in high schools; and establish myself as an independent researcher at a Danish university."

title: Elucidating genetic programs in hematopoietic stem cells
summary: The project aim is to use CRISPR-based tools to study the genetic programs that govern the plasticity of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. Increased insights into this phenomenon might bring new treatment modalities to regenerative medicine and hematological disorders.

title: Checkpoint Inhibitor Bioassay for Next-Generation Immunotherapy Nanomedicines
summary: Optimise immunotherapy designs for preclinical evaluation

title: Business model innovation for the SDGs - drivers, barriers and success practices
summary: The project aims to investigate how business model innovation can contribute to realization of the SDGs, and it will focus on the drivers, barriers and success practices related to the adoption of business model innovation for the SDGs. The project also aims to develop a research-based SDG-oriented business model simulator, which will be used by the research group to model business model innovation for the SDGs through system dynamics simulations, case study and action research.

title: Building a Mobile Eye Tracking Infrastructure in Denmark
summary: We aim to build a mobile eye tracking infrastructure at the Interacting Minds Centre  IMC . Mobile eye tracking is an increasingly popular noninvasive method for collecting behavioural data in a wide variety of laboratory and field settings. Modern mobile eye tracking allows researchers to collect data during real time social interactions, high activity endeavours  such as sports or dance , and ecological field settings with high degrees of freedom for research participants. A modern mobile eye tracking infrastructure would hugely benefit our ability to take laboratory studies on humans attention into the field. The IMC is currently DK s largest network of researchers investigating social interaction, perception   cognition and is an ideal base for state-of-the-art mobile eye tracking technology in Denmark.

title: Broadband THz Laser Spectroscopy of Weakly Bound Cluster Molecules
summary: In the proposed project, we plan to combine a low-temperature cluster spectroscopy approach based on doped para-H2 quantum crystals with a newly developed commercial broadband THz laser system and construct a world-class THz cluster spectroscopy facility at DTU. The resulting THz cluster spectrometer would be the first of its kind in the world and would improve the experimental sensitivity throughout the THz region and the spectral resolution with orders of magnitude simultaneously. The establishment of the proposed THz cluster spectroscopy facility at DTU Chemistry would both strengthen the fundamental research within chemical physics and the interplay between theory and experiment within DTU and between the Danish universities as the experimental findings would be highly relevant for the theoretical chemistry community  see attached project description . This world-class experimental facility would furthermore help to attract talented PhD students and postdoctoral researchers from abroad and make DTU Chemistry an attractive partner in European training networks.

title: Unravelling the secrets of spintronic materials with neutron scattering
summary: So-called antiferromagnetic spintronics have the potential to outperform present-day computing and storage technology by orders of magnitude, but only if the right materials are found. With this proposal, I wish to investigate a family of materials that has shown promising properties in this direction. Most excitingly, these materials are functional at room temperature, which is a rarity in condensed matter research. I will synthesize new members of this family of materials and investigate their spintronic properties, mainly using neutron scattering techniques.

title: Understanding the molecular basis of NAD-depleting toxins in bacteria
summary: The aim of the project is to understand how specific bacterial toxins function at the molecular level, thus providing a detailed insight into this mechanism of survival, which is common among pathogenic bacteria.

title: Understanding the mechanisms of gender disparity in financial choices
summary: Gender disparity has been documented in both household asset management as well as their liability management. Our project seeks to identify where the gender disparity arises, how mechanisms financial mistakes are made, and the characteristics of individuals explaining the behavior. Understanding mechanisms of discrimination are of the essence to have the ability to design policies to reduce discrimination.

title: Ultra small samples directly on CO2 for Accelerator Mass Spectrometry  AMS    a first step towards 14CO2 dating of methane from marine sediments
summary: The accelerator mass spectrometer  AMS  instrument facility at Department of Physics and Astronomy are unique to Denmark and is comparable with some of the best international radiocarbon laboratories in e.g. Sweden, Norway, Germany, Poland and the UK. However, we still lack the capacity for ultra-small samples, which is necessary to bring the Danish AMS facility into the World s absolute elite. This suggested upgrade will bring the AARAMS 14C instrumental setup in-line with the state-of-the-art instruments on the market, making our facility among the World leading facilities. Specifically, we aim at having instrument capabilities to engage in research into the mineralization dynamics of the large amounts of carbon stored in the frozen soils and marine sediments of the Arctic in collaboration with other research groups, i.e. release of carbon dioxide and methane. The 14C concentration of the released methane and carbon dioxide from marine sediments are essential to infer the carbon origin and the time scales at which these greenhouse gases are released. Furthermore, upgrading the AMS for direct 14C CO2 analysis will provide the full benefit of our 14C in-situ extraction line as the conversion to solid samples may introduce contaminants from the modern  14C active  atmosphere. In-situ 14C has previously been supported the Carlsberg Foundation.

pi_affiliation: University of Copenhagen, Niels Bohr Institute
title: Topology in the Correlated Fe-Based Superconductors
summary: This project studies whether topological states, useful for quantum computation, can appear in correlated materials. This will be accomplished using three complementary approaches. These involve the derivation of a minimal model, a description of how various correlation effects impact the presence of topological states, and finally, the design of an experiment to probe the existence of topological states. The successful completion of this project will introduce a new family of materials as possible hosts for topological states, and address the fundamental question of how topological states arise from correlated electrons. This will expand the range of materials useful as constituents in quantum computers.

title: RootScan
summary: In our research group, we currently focus on alleviating the root knowledge gap in ecology. Roots play pivotal roles for terrestrial ecosystem functionality, as roots determine plant water and nutrient uptake, and drive ecosystem carbon storage. Yet, roots remain one of the most understudied and least understood ecosystem components. Through current Carlsberg postdoc re-integration and EU MSCA fellowship funding, we quantify above- and belowground plant functional responses to experimental climate change in the Arctic. However, we spend substantial excess time on manual image data validation and cleaning due to scanning artefacts arising from using non-specialized instruments. Consequently, we are seeking funds to purchase a state-of-the-art optical scanner built exclusively for root analyses. This automated instrument will greatly reduce root data acquisition time and it will eliminate scanning artefacts that potentially bias results. Ultimately, these funds will allow us to focus our research efforts on producing high quality, novel root data that are a top research priority for the broader scientific community.

pi_affiliation: University of Copenhagen, Niels Bohr Institute
title: Repair and regulation in DNA damage response
summary: This project aims at understanding the fundamental interplay between the reparation of DNA damage, stimulated by the formation of foci, and the regulation of cell state, mediated by the transcription factor p53. By combining mathematical models and analysis of experimental data, I intend to discover how the two different aspects of DNA damage response can affect each other and how an optimal interplay is achieved.

title: Protoclusters  and Supermassive Black Holes
summary: The project aims to shed new light on how galaxy clusters grow as a function of cosmic time and how the supermassive black hole at the centre of the cluster affects the cluster evolution.

title: Presence lab
summary: Virtual reality  VR  lets users explore computer-generated worlds by wearing head-mounted displays and moving their bodies. For VR to be successful, users must experience a sense of being there, so-called presence. However, presence remains difficult to study because it requires precise tracking of users  movement in the real world and because multi-user setups are difficult to create. We will establish Presence Lab, which allows the motion of multiple users to be tracked with low latency and high accuracy. Thereby, movements in the real and virtual worlds will be perfectly synchronized across users. Presence Lab will thus allow us to chart the conditions required for presence to occur --- a central, unsolved research problem in computer science and psychology --- and to create new VR experiences by sharing worlds and bodies across users. The lab will be state-of-the-art and serve researchers within University of Copenhagen and across the Copenhagen area.

title: Pandemiens paavirkning af danskernes miljoeadfaerd og holdninger til klima. Der soeges 81.500 kr. til udfoerelse af en repraesentativ spoergeskemaundersoegelse af danskernes CO2-fodaftryk samt holdninger til spoergsmaal relateret til klima.
summary: Formaalet er ved hjaelp af et komparativt datagrundlag fra efteraaret 2019 at undersoege, hvorledes COVID-19 pandemien har paavirket danskernes miljoeadfaerd samt holdninger til klimarelaterede spoergsmål. Mere specifikt oensker vi at besvare foelgende to problemstillinger: 1. Hvordan samfundskriser i generel forstand paavirker miljoeadfaerd og holdninger til klima-spoergsmål samt 2. hvorvidt krisen har aendret danskernes tanker om grundlaeggende livsvaerdier og forbrug.

title: Optimization of Cryo-EM characterization pipeline for biomolecular nanostructures
summary: The aim of the project is to establish an efficient cryo-EM characterization pipeline, since high-resolution structural characterization is an essential component of the development of improved biomolecular nanostructures for downstream applications.

title: NMR-based lipidomics for disease detection
summary: We wish to establish NMR-based lipidomics with orders of magnitude better sensitivity and resolution than existing methods.

title: Measuring macromolecular interactions under native conditions
summary: Multivalent macromolecular interactions underlie a vast range of biological processes. Implementation of the FIDAbio system at iNANO will allow us and many other users to accurately determine the kinetics and dynamics of macromolecular interactions under native conditions.

title: Masculine Identities in Classical Greece
summary: The project examines examples of men in Greek literature who adopt behaviour or values which are considered feminine. These examples of extraordinary or marginalised male behaviour and sexuality offer an alternative history of masculinity, which has been almost entirely neglected. The project shows how effeminacy and femininity play a crucial role in epic and drama and are taken on in the philosophical creation of the self, particularly in Plato. This provides a corrective to traditional histories of masculinity but also offers to ground current debates about male gender identity and sexuality historically in the Ancient Greek world.

title: Malting and beer production in Danish Prehistory. By means of SEM of charred archaeological cereal grains, the aim is to shed light on the chronological and geographical occurrence of malting and beer brewing in Danish prehistory
summary: To identify malt and beer production in Danish prehistory

title: Infrastructure for Multi- and Hyperspectral Image Acquisition
summary: This proposal aims to create a state-of-the art customized infrastructure in both Multi- and Hyper Spectral Imaging  MSI and HSI  to support the growing research on medieval literature and manuscripts at SDU.

title: I-HANK: The International Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian model
summary: "Why are booms and busts in economic activity so closely connected across countries? While this question is crucial for designing economic stabilization policies, it has challenged macroeconomists for decades. Existing economic models struggle to account for the high degrees of co-movement of economic activity across industrialized countries, and thus tend to understate the importance of foreign economic developments for small open economies such as Denmark. This may lead to misguided economic policy recommendations. The last decade has witnessed a small revolution within macroeconomics, with an emerging literature studying business cycles through the lens of macroeconomic models featuring heterogeneity in income and wealth levels across households; so-called HANK models. These models feature a powerful feedback loop between unemployment risk, income inequality, and aggregate demand. My main hypothesis in this project is that a fall in exports can trigger this loop. With very few exceptions, the existing HANK literature has focused exclusively on models of closed economies. My aim of this research endeavor is to develop an International Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian model, I-HANK, and investigate the hypothesis that such a model can resolve the puzzle of international economic co-movement described above. As a part in this, I wish to establish an international network of young researchers."

title: How does host genome determine the microbiome?
summary: "In a typical animal such as ourselves, bacterial cells greatly outnumber our own. Animal associated bacteria; ie. the microbiome; greatly influence animal health and function, and affect a growing list of traits, including behaviour, nutrition and disease. This project will use cutting-edge genetic manipulation, together with advanced sequencing technology, to determine how an animal controls which bacteria comprise the microbiome. It will exploit the unique biology of a new model system, the planarian flatworms, to genetically transform individuals without manipulating microbiome, allowing us to truly isolate the role of host genetics from the environmental effects. These experiments are not possible in any other system, and stand to revolutionise the study of host-microbiome interactions."

title: How do soil invertebrates survive thermal extremes?
summary: The project aims at linking physiological responses to the performance of individuals   e.g. behaviour, predation, growth and reproduction  and survival of populations in real environments. We therefore apply for funding to buy a large, programmable climate chamber allowing us to simulate natural diurnal fluctuations and cooling heating rates. This equipment will benefit the quality and possibilities of our research considerably.

title: How a new layer of genetic control boosts plant seed germination
summary: This project investigates how a global boost in protein synthesis capacity mediated by covalent modification of messenger RNA potentiates plant seed germination.

title: From plants to animals - understanding inter-kingdom host-shifts of fungal pathogens
summary: This project aim to use fungi from the genus Colletotrichum to unravel the fundamental question of how fungi can colonize new host niches and switch from plant to insect pathogenicity, or go from mutualistic endophytism to plant pathogenicity.

title: Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy,   FLIM, for chemical and metabolic imaging in microbial systems
summary: To acquire a modulated laser system that will enable FLIM analyses with ultrashort lifetimes, i.e., nano- to microseconds, with the goal to develop and apply fluorescent probes for imaging metabolic states of microbes in their natural chemical gradient environment

title: Fast Protein Liquid Chromatography for Protein Purification
summary: It is important that there is a fast protein liquid chromatography for protein purification, i.e.,  FPLC,  at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, University of Southern Denmark, because the department must maintain its completive profile for research and education in the fields of enzyme catalysis, protein chemistry, and pharmacy. In particular, the department has five large international groups, which highly depend on the availability of the FPLC. Without it, their research progress will be significantly affected. Moreover, the access to FPLC at the department will contribute to high quality education to chemistry and pharmacy students by providing their hands on experience with proteins in labs.

title: Epitranscriptomic sequencing
summary: The application concerns the procurement of an Ion Torrent sequencer for applications of the RiboMeth-seq method developed in our laboratory as well as the development of new sequencing-based methods for molecular biology. Using RiboMeth-seq, we have discovered distinct changes in the pattern of 112 ribose methylations in functionally important parts of the human ribosome during physiological processes e.g. T cell activation as well as in pathological settings, in particular in cancer. These changes impact the decoding of genetic information by impacting protein synthesis. Our aim is to understand specific roles of key ribose methylations in mRNA recruitment and ribosome performance. A key hypothesis is that the ribosome balance translation speed and fidelity through RNA modifications that impact the ribosomes conformational flexibility.

title: Electron Microscopy for Quantum Materials and Nanoscience
summary: "Electron microscopy is an essential tool for investigating man-made and natural materials at the highest level of detail; one can image crystalline solids with atomic resolution, determine the morphology of nano-structured materials and reveal the detailed structure of biomolecules. With materials research in mind we propose the acquisition of transmission electron microscope at KU, to replace an instrument from 1991. The main projects address quantum materials and nanostructured catalysts, respectively - two highly active areas in physics and chemistry. The facility will be open to other users and half the necessary funding has already been secured."

title: EarthHologenomics: unveiling global patterns of gut microbiome-animal interactions in light of environmental variation
summary: Perform the first global mapping of spatial variation of gut microbiome-animal interactions, to extract patterns that are likely to shape ecological and evolutionary processes.

title: Deep sub-wavelength conductivity mapping of nanoscale domains in 2D materials  DEEP-MAP
summary: We apply for funding for a terahertz time-domain extension of a near-field spectrometer. The aim of the project is to investigate conductivity phenomena on the 10-nanometer length scale to find the influence of nanoscale irregular structure  grain boundaries, impurities  on macroscopic properties of 2D materials.

summary: Characterization of purified membrane proteins with focus on electrophysiology at the single molecule level

summary: To enable in-situ hydration studies using diffraction and imaging techniques at DanMAX.
